def: The origin measured by a clock's time_point: a time_point stores only a duration, meaning "how far from the epoch". The epoch of system_clock is 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC; the epochs of steady_clock and file_clock are unspecified. Two clocks have different epochs, so their time_points cannot be directly compared or subtracted.

What a "clock" type must provide: four member types rep, period, duration, time_point; a bool constant is_steady usable in constant expressions; and a static function now() returning the current time_point. The is_clock trait checks at least for the presence of these names.

On top of Cpp17Clock it additionally requires: rep, duration, and time_point are comparable, swappable, and meet the numeric type requirements (so their operations do not throw), now() does not throw, and time_point::clock recursively meets these requirements. The clocks used by the timeout functions of the standard thread library are all such clocks.

The length of time between two adjacent "counting units" of a duration, in seconds, represented by a compile-time rational ratio. The tick period of duration<long long, milli> is 1/1000 second; count() returns the number of ticks, not the number of seconds.

A time measure counted from 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC that does not count leap seconds: every day has exactly 86400 seconds. sys_time is, by the standard's specification, Unix time, so sys_days and civil calendar dates can be converted with pure arithmetic.

A second inserted (or deleted) to keep UTC aligned with the Earth's rotation. sys_time does not count leap seconds, while utc_time does; the difference between them is the total number of leap seconds inserted since 1970. The leap second table is provided with the time zone database (tzdb::leap_seconds).

A time point stored as separate fields such as year, month, and day, such as year_month_day. It makes arithmetic by year or month and field access easy, but adding or subtracting days is inconvenient; by contrast, sys_days is a "serial" time point (an integer count of days), with fast day arithmetic. The two can be converted into each other.

The family of time_points local_time<Duration> parameterized by the pseudo-clock local_t: it represents "the wall-clock time in some time zone not yet specified". It has full time_point arithmetic but no now(), and cannot be mixed with sys_time; converting it to UTC must go through some time_zone.

The locale actually used by chrono formatting: when the format spec has no L option, the "C" locale is always used; with L, the locale passed to the formatting function is used, or the global locale if none is passed.

An updated time zone database that the implementation may obtain while the program is running. It does not affect the program automatically: only when reload_tzdb() is called is it pushed to the front of the tzdb_list, and remote_version() can query its version.
